# Final answer

## What I changed

Only the last layer: `fc.weight` and `fc.bias`. No other tensor is edited.

The new decision direction (row 1 minus row 0) is built in closed form from the four group means of the 2,048 avgpool features over the practice set:

- `d_bird` = waterbird minus landbird mean, averaged over the two backgrounds.
- `d_bg` = water minus land mean, averaged over the two bird classes.
- `v = d_bird − (d_bird·d_bg / d_bg·d_bg)·d_bg`, rescaled so that bird identity is worth 16 logits, as in the original model.
- Bias: the midpoint between the two class means along `v`, plus 0.25 logits toward "waterbird".

The common mode of the two fc rows is left untouched. By construction the background mean shift along `v` is exactly zero.

## Results

All 50 forward passes are used. The final pass verified the submitted tensors on the full practice set:

| | LL | LW | WL | WW | worst | mean |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Original | 99.4 | 82.6 | 72.9 | 96.2 | 72.9 | 97.7 |
| Submitted edit (practice, in-sample) | 96.8 | 91.9 | 94.0 | 94.0 | 91.9 | 95.95 |
| Held-out, centre crop (offset 0) | 97.4 | 92.3 | 92.5 | 93.2 | 92.3 | 96.25 |
| Held-out, mirrored (offset 0) | 96.8 | 92.9 | 92.5 | 94.0 | 92.5 | 96.0 |
| Held-out, shifted crop (offset 0) | 96.8 | 92.7 | 92.5 | 93.2 | 92.5 | 95.8 |

The held-out rows were run with the bias at the midpoint, with each image scored by an edit built from the other half of the practice set. With the submitted +0.25 offset, the view-averaged held-out figures are about 96.8 / 91.9 / 93.0 / 93.5.

Paired against the original on the practice set, the submitted edit fixes 28 waterbird/land images and breaks none, and fixes 46 landbird/water images and breaks 3. It costs 12 landbird/land and 3 waterbird/water images.

I expect roughly worst group 92% and mean 96% on the test set. My rough estimate of meeting both targets is about 0.9; the main risk is sampling noise in the two 642-image waterbird groups.

## What goes wrong in the network

- **The last layer reads the background.** Switching land to water moves the margin by 8.1 logits, half the bird's own 16. The original direction is essentially `0.114·d_bird + 0.068·d_bg` (84% of its squared norm lies in that plane).
- **The background contribution is diffuse.** The top 10 channels carry 12% of it and it takes about 800 for 95%, so deleting channels cannot work; a direction-level edit is needed.
- **The background is linearly readable from layer1 on; bird evidence is built in layer4.** The two directions are orthogonal at the end of layer3 (cosine 0.04) and become aligned in layer4.1 and layer4.2 (0.30, then 0.57).
- **The last block fuses them.** layer4.2 writes 59% of the background shift and 87% of the bird shift that fc reads.
- **One direction at the end of layer3 feeds the shortcut.** Hiding it from layer4.0 removes 84% of fc's background shift. Injecting ±1 unit of it (two running-mean tensors only) steers waterbird/land accuracy from 38% to 94%.
- **Bird and scene enter layer4.2 as separable signals.** Blinding its first convolution to the scene direction gives a bird classifier with fc untouched (worst group 91.0% at strength 1.5). Blinding it to the bird direction gives a background classifier (7–10% on the mismatched groups). A same-size control direction does nothing.

## Evidence that the edit acts on that mechanism

- **Dose-response in the real network.** Worst group is 84.8 / 88.0 / 92.7 / 88.2 for cancellation strength 0 / 0.5 / 1 / 1.5 (bias at the midpoint). Projecting out a random direction with the same overlap leaves it at 84.4.
- **Composite images.** Swapping only the surroundings moves the original's margin by 6.2–8.3 logits and the edited model's by −0.9 to +0.15. Swapping only the bird moves both by 15.0. Pooled accuracy over three composite sets goes from 95.8 / 83.2 / 77.4 / 94.7 to 91.6 / 92.6 / 93.2 / 93.2.
- **Bird removed.** The original calls 92% of water scenes and 14% of land scenes "waterbird"; the edited model calls 61% and 53%.
- **Per-position evidence (96 random images).** The scene vote falls from 7.6 to 0.35 logits while the bird vote is essentially unchanged (17.6 to 16.8).

## What I tried and did not keep

- **Fitted last layers.** Logistic and shrunk-Fisher refits with 2,048 free weights held out at worst group about 90%, and worse when weakly regularised. In a nested selection the closed-form direction was chosen in 10 of 12 splits.
- **Upstream edits as part of the repair.** Blinding layer4.1, layer4.2, or the layer3 or layer2 scene direction, with fc re-derived, gave no gain that generalised. The layer2 cut helped four practice waterbird/land images in a dose-dependent way but failed two independent composite checks (4 fixed, 7 broken), so I rejected it.
- **Bias offset.** Estimated pass probability is flat for offsets from 0 to +0.5; I chose +0.25 as the centre of that plateau. Offset 0 scores 97.6 / 92.7 / 93.2 / 94.0 in-sample and is saved as `work/best_1`.

## Limits

About 7–8% of each hard group remains wrong. These are mostly bird-evidence failures that no background fix addresses:

- Species labelled "waterbird" that look like landbirds: all 8 pewee-like practice images are wrong, and the features cannot separate them from flycatchers.
- Tiny or oddly posed birds.
- Water photos that contain real ducks.

The submitted tensors are in `work/edited` (identical to `work/best_2`); `work/notes.md` logs every pass.
